drills.q: State Resilience4j's fixed AOP decorator order from outermost to innermost.
drills.a: Retry -> CircuitBreaker -> RateLimiter -> TimeLimiter -> Bulkhead (Bulkhead innermost, closest to the actual method call).

drills.q: True or false: reordering @Retry and @CircuitBreaker annotations on a Spring method changes which one executes first.
drills.a: False. The aspect order is hardcoded by the library regardless of annotation declaration order; override only via explicit *AspectOrder configuration properties.
SemaphoreBulkhead (default, counting semaphore on caller's thread) and ThreadPoolBulkhead (dedicated ThreadPoolExecutor + bounded queue).

drills.q: A team configures limitForPeriod=20, limitRefreshPeriod=1s expecting a smooth ~20 req/s cap, but downstream still sees short traffic spikes near 40 requests in 20ms. Explain why.
drills.a: Resilience4j's RateLimiter is a fixed-window algorithm, not a token bucket -- permissions reset in a step function at the start of each cycle. A full 20-permit burst at the very end of cycle N followed immediately by a full 20-permit burst at the start of cycle N+1 is fully compliant with the configuration, producing up to ~2x the nominal rate in the boundary window.

drills.q: A @CircuitBreaker(fallbackMethod="fallbackPrice") never invokes its fallback -- the original exception always propagates. What are the two most likely causes to check, in order?
drills.a: First, a fallback method signature mismatch (must exactly match the original method's parameters plus a trailing Throwable/exception type) -- registration fails silently at startup, check startup logs. Second, if the signature is correct, check whether the thrown exception is in the module's configured ignoreExceptions list -- ignored exceptions deliberately don't trigger fallback logic, which is working as intended, not a bug.

drills.q: A legacy blocking SOAP client with no internal timeout is protected only by a SemaphoreBulkhead. Under a stuck downstream, does the bulkhead prevent service degradation? Why or why not.
drills.a: Not fully -- a semaphore can only block NEW calls from acquiring a permit once the limit is reached; it cannot interrupt a call already in flight. A stuck call holds its permit indefinitely, so the service still degrades, just more slowly than with no bulkhead at all. The fix is pairing it with an explicit timeout or switching to ThreadPoolBulkhead, which can interrupt the executing thread.

drills.q: Why is Retry placed outermost in the default Resilience4j order rather than innermost, wrapping only the raw downstream call?
drills.a: Retry needs to see the outcome of the entire inner stack (bulkhead rejection, rate-limit rejection, breaker fast-fail, or genuine failure) as ONE attempt, so one logical failure triggers one retry decision. If Retry were innermost, each retry attempt would separately trip the bulkhead/limiter/breaker, amplifying one logical failure into multiple recorded failures at each inner layer.

drills.q: Design the resilience config for a downstream pricing call with p99 spikes to 4s under load but rare outright failures, where the caller owes the user 2s total end to end.
drills.a: TimeLimiter bounding each attempt well below the 2s budget (e.g. ~800ms, leaving room for one retry plus fallback), CircuitBreaker with slowCallRateThreshold/slowCallDurationThreshold configured (this IS the slow-success case), Retry with a small maxAttempts (2) and full-jitter backoff (aggressive retry on an already-struggling downstream adds load at the worst time), a SemaphoreBulkhead sized via Little's Law if the client is reactive, and a fallback serving last-known-good cached price rather than a bare error.

drills.q: Explain the specific architectural flaw in Hystrix's thread-pool-per-command default that Resilience4j's module design addresses.
drills.a: Hystrix mandated a dedicated thread pool per command/dependency with no opt-out, so a service calling many dependencies paid real memory and context-switch cost multiplying with dependency count, purely for isolation it may not have always needed. Resilience4j decouples bulkheading from the other modules and defaults to the cheap SemaphoreBulkhead, making the expensive ThreadPoolBulkhead an explicit, per-dependency opt-in instead of a universal default.

drills.q: Both an Envoy service mesh and an application's @Retry(maxAttempts=3) are configured to retry the same downstream call. What's the actual attempt count under a total failure, and what's the fix?
drills.a: Up to 3x3=9 attempts for one logical call -- retries multiply across layers rather than adding. Fix: pick exactly one layer to own retry for that call path (typically in-process if the retry decision needs to know idempotency/business semantics, mesh-level if it's a pure transport concern) and explicitly disable retry at the other layer.
